conviction_note: No decisive unpriced number found: the company beats its own guide by about 2% as a habit (priced), the one primary-document negative is a sharp RPO growth deceleration in the 10-K that management has an on-record explanation for, and the stock has run +30.6% in 20 days to above every average target into a neutral skew, so p_up sits just under 50 (48) on an option-implied scale of about 11.5 points; findings sum -0.4, scaled number -0.46, they agree in sign and size.
bar: Company Q1 FY27 guide (Aug 4 2026 8-K ex.99.1): total revenue $159.3-160.3m (mid $159.8m), SaaS $123.7-124.7m, non-GAAP op income $33.4-34.4m, non-GAAP EPS $0.39-0.41; FY27 total revenue $656.5-660.5m, EPS $1.58-1.62 — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001565687/000156568726000065/inta-20260630xex991.htm. Street consensus could not be sourced from two agreeing current sources (EarningsWhispers still shows a stale pre-guide $0.34 / $157.66m; MarketBeat reported pre-guide consensus $0.28 / $157.4m), so the guide midpoint is the bar and sizes are kept small. The Q4 FY26 print beat the top of its guide on every line (total $152.5m vs $149.1-150.1m, SaaS $115.0m vs $113.1-114.1m, EPS $0.41 vs $0.36-0.38), so the effective whisper is above the guide midpoint, roughly $161-162m / $0.42-0.43. Cloud ARR (the metric the stock trades on) has no company guide; to hold 29% YoY it needs about $517.8m (net new about $22m vs $17.1m in Q1 FY26), to hold 28% about $513.8m.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,716,096 shares, 4.02% of float, 5.1 days to cover, settlement 2026-10-15, down 12.4% from 3,101,714 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/INTA/short-interest/, read 2026-10-27; Equibles shows 3.5% of float, 5.1 days, falling: https://equibles.com/stocks/INTA). Not a crowded short; shorts have been covering into the rally, so the squeeze fuel is mostly spent. Option market: 25-delta skew -0.09 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.26 on only 306 contracts total, ATM spread 34% of mid (thin chain), event-implied move 11.48%. Tape: +30.6% over 20 sessions, +2.66% over 5, 4.2% below the 52-week high, 140% above the 52-week low; reported closes $37.60 on 2026-10-07 and a $48.01 high on 2026-10-23, then about -3% on 2026-10-27 into the print. The share price ($46) sits above the average analyst target ($39.14, MarketBeat 2026-10-23; ratings 4 Buy / 4 Hold / 2 Sell).

findings.finding: The FY26 10-K shows remaining performance obligations of $833.0m at 2026-06-30, up 15.7% YoY, after four straight quarters of 26-27% YoY growth (Jun-25 $719.7m +27.0%, Dec-25 $777.1m +26.3%, Mar-26 $791.4m +27.3%); the Q4 sequential add was $41.6m against $98.2m a year earlier. The Q1 10-Q, normally filed the same day as the release, will show Sep-26 RPO. Q1 is seasonally flat (Sep-25 was $715.2m, -$4.5m QoQ), so a repeat puts YoY RPO growth near 16%, which would confirm the deceleration. The market's expectation sits on cloud ARR growth of about 29%, not on RPO.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RPO has not been a headline line in any of the last six reactions in the baseline; the Aug 4 2026 +12.75% reaction preceded the 10-K (Aug 14) in which the deceleration first appeared, and the stock has risen roughly 15% since that filing without it being cited anywhere found.
findings.why_not_priced: Intapp reports ARR and NRR as headline KPIs, and RPO appears only in the 10-K/10-Q revenue note. No preview, target change or article found since Aug 14 mentions it. If it were priced, some analyst note in the October target raises (Barclays to $38, UBS to $46) would cite backlog. It is partly explained, which caps the size: on the Aug 4 call the CFO said many on-prem clients are shortening contracts to one year or less ahead of cloud migration. That compresses multi-year license RPO without implying weaker cloud demand.
findings.independence: Same company documents. CFO commentary on shortened on-prem terms and license revenue -25% in Q4 (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2945294) explains rather than corroborates it. Cloud ARR growth slowing from 31% (Mar-26, https://s206.q4cdn.com/284424942/files/doc_earnings/2026/q3/earnings-result/Q3-26-Press-Release.pdf) to 29% (Jun-26) points mildly the same way.

findings.finding: Intapp habitually prints above the top of its own quarterly guide. Q4 FY26 total revenue was $152.5m against $149.1-150.1m (+1.9% vs the midpoint), SaaS $115.0m against $113.1-114.1m, and non-GAAP EPS $0.41 against $0.36-0.38. A repeat on the Q1 guide (total $159.3-160.3m, SaaS $123.7-124.7m, EPS $0.39-0.41) implies about $162m total, about $125.5m SaaS (+29% YoY vs $97.5m), and about $0.43 EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats of a similar size drew +12.75% (Aug 4 2026, $0.41 vs $0.36 plus a guide above consensus) and -4.19% (May 5 2026, beat by $0.01). The headline beat alone has not set the sign; the guide and cloud ARR have.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. A modest beat inside the company's own pattern is what the Street models, so this lands inside what the company guided and should be sized toward 0. It is filed because a judge needs the effective bar: a print merely at the guide midpoint would read as a miss.
findings.independence: Q4 actuals from the Aug 4 2026 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001565687/000156568726000065/inta-20260630xex991.htm), a different document from the Q4 guide in the May 5 release.

findings.finding: The stock ran +30.6% in 20 sessions, from $37.60 on Oct 7 to a $48.01 high on Oct 23, on a sector-wide software rerating with no company-specific catalyst found. It now trades at $46, above the average analyst target of $39.14; Barclays raised its target only to $38 at Underweight on Oct 12. Short interest is 4% of float and falling, so there is no squeeze bid to cushion a disappointment. The setup asks Q1 to justify a rerating rather than to clear the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline does not record pre-print run-ups. The Feb 3 2026 print fell -13.2% after the stock had held up into the sector's AI-disruption sell-off. Six-print history: 2 up, 4 down, median absolute move 9.67%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is public, so this is about asymmetry, not hidden information. Skew is flat (-0.09) and put/call OI is 0.26, so options are not paying for downside after a 30% move. If the market were braced for a sell-the-news reaction, puts would be bid. The sector move was index-led: the software index hit 2026 highs on Oct 6 as AI-disruption fears faded. That makes INTA's extra rise a beta re-rating that a soft cloud ARR number or an unraised FY guide would test.
findings.independence: Sector context from Reuters via US News, 2026-10-06 (https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-10-06/us-software-stocks-scale-fresh-2026-highs-as-ai-disruption-worries-fade); Barclays Underweight with a $38 target on 2026-10-12 (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/nebenwerte/barclays-lifts-target-for-intapp-stock-to-usd-38-00/70333435); short interest from MarketBeat's short-interest page. These are different sources pointing the same way, but none is a company number.

findings.finding: Celeste (agentic AI) momentum went into Q1. In Q4, AI was over 20% of net new bookings and roughly doubled sequentially (CFO, Aug 4 call). During the quarter Intapp announced DealCloud-with-Celeste selections by Forvis Mazars Capital Advisors (Sep 22), Practus LLP (Sep 1) and Carr, Riggs & Ingram M&A Advisors (Oct 20). OpenAI's Sep 17 Astra for Law launch named Intapp as an integration partner, and Intapp shipped a Celeste plug-in for ChatGPT Enterprise. If disclosed on the call, a further rise in the AI share of bookings, or a first Celeste ARR figure, supports the FY27 guide and the $1bn ARR by FY29 target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Aug 4 2026 the first AI-bookings disclosure, plus a guide above consensus, came with +12.75%. The Feb 3 2026 print (-13.2%) came amid the AI-disruption sell-off in legal software, so this name reacts in both directions to the AI narrative.
findings.why_not_priced: The named wins are mid-market advisory and accounting firms, not Am Law 100 names, and no aggregator quantifies them. The OpenAI partnership was public on Sep 17 and is plausibly part of the October rerating, which caps the size. What the market cannot yet see is the Q1 AI bookings share or a Celeste monetisation number. If that were priced, the sell-side targets would not still average below the share price.
findings.independence: AI bookings figure from the Q4 call transcript (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2945294). OpenAI launch naming Intapp as a partner, independently reported by LawNext (https://www.lawnext.com/2026/09/yesterday-came-openais-launch-into-legal-now-come-the-litany-of-vendor-integrations.html). Customer wins from Intapp's own newsroom. The newsroom and the call are both company sources.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 investment-banking fees, reported Oct 13-14 after Intapp last spoke, rose at most large banks: Goldman +21% with record advisory fees of $1.65bn (+18%), JPMorgan about +14%, Bank of America -11%. Banks described a late-September pause but robust backlogs. This is a demand proxy for DealCloud's capital-markets and advisory client base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to this line; it is a proxy for one segment of the client base.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public macro, and transmission to Intapp is unconfirmed by the company. Filed small, as a proxy. It matters only if management cites improving capital-markets demand in the FY27 commentary.
findings.independence: JPMorgan's September guidance of mid-to-high-teens IB fee growth (https://pulse2.com/jpmorgan-expects-q3-investment-banking-fees-and-markets-revenue-to-rise-mid-to-high-teens/amp/), a different source. Single secondary source for the reported figures.

findings.finding: Thomson Reuters' Q2 2026 Law Firm Financial Index (Aug 10, 2026) shows US law-firm technology and knowledge-management spending up 11.6% YoY, 8.7% per lawyer, with demand up about 3% and rates up more than 7%. Intapp's largest vertical is still funding software spend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to this series.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August and an industry proxy, so filed small. It argues against the idea that AI tools are cannibalising law-firm software budgets in calendar Q2-Q3, which is Intapp's Q4-Q1.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 LFFI showed overhead +8.3%, tied to AI and technology investment (https://thelawreporters.com/rising-ai-costs-weigh-on-us-law-firm-profits-2026). Same publisher, different quarter.

findings.finding: On the capital-return line, about $75m remained on the $200m buyback authorised on Jan 29, 2026, at 2026-06-30. Cash was $162.8m, and on Jul 7, 2026 a new undrawn $150m UBS senior secured revolver replaced the $100m JPMorgan facility. Intapp bought back 8.4m shares for $275.2m in FY26 and announced its prior programmes alongside prints (Aug 2025, Jan 2026), so a new authorisation with the Q1 release is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2025 print came with a $150m buyback and +15.52%. The Jan 29 2026 $200m authorisation preceded the Feb 3 print, which fell -13.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: The remaining-authorisation figure sits in the 10-K body, not in the release. The revolver is undrawn and there is no sign of distress: cash flow is positive and the covenants restrict repurchases rather than signalling a need for cash. The money funds flexibility for buybacks or M&A, so the sign is positive or zero. Buying at $46, against $33 on average in FY26, is less accretive, which caps the size.
findings.independence: FY26 repurchase total of $275.2m for 8.4m shares, from the Aug 4 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001565687/000156568726000065/inta-20260630xex991.htm). Same company, different document.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and pre-planned under 10b5-1, so it carries almost no information about the quarter. Filed at near zero for completeness.
findings.independence: MarketBeat tally of the same Form 4s (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-intapp-nasdaq-inta-hits-new-12-month-high-heres-why-2026-10-23/). Same underlying filings.

baseline_tension: The findings agree with the flat skew: they are balanced, with a small negative lean that comes from the +30.6% run-up and the RPO deceleration rather than from the quarter's numbers, which should clear the guide. Nothing found argues the option market's 11.5% is too large or too small.

Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the RPO finding moved from -0.8 to -0.7, because the CFO's shortened on-prem contract explanation is on record
Lesson 7 (positioning, short interest checked): the run-up/positioning finding moved from -1.5 to -1.2; short interest of 4% is not crowded, but the finding rests on no document
